items.title: Brunies Brother Band Interview, 1957-10-19
items.q: I got a man by the name of Dudley Mecham to put lyrics to.

ctx.x: How did that come to the degree of the six? Well, we wrote Angry in Bluxy here.

Jules Kazard, my brother Henry and I, and when I went to Chicago, and when I was in California, my brother George called me and told me he was going to make a record of it. Him and Paul, Paul Mez and George and him, with the New Orleans Rhythm Kings, and they made a record of Angry. So then I got busy and got lyrics to it, and I got a man by the name of Dudley Mecham to put lyrics to. Where is he? Is he here? He's in Chicago. Chicago. Chicago. Chicago.

items.title: Brunies Brother Band Interview, 1957-10-19
items.q: Then one more that Abby told us about. Rudy. Rudy. He played string bass. Then my sister, Data, played guitar.

ctx.x: . Now we have some time. Yeah, it's going all right now. If you can just tell us first, forget your name on Abby, so we know. Okay, this is Abby Brunus speaking. And now these folks are here wanting to know how I started. It's been so long, it's hard to remember. We're back there in 1908. When were you born? In 1900. And we started out, I think we were the first school band in the United States. There was only three pieces. And the three pieces consist of Emmett Rogers, George Brunus, and myself. And then we...…

. He played it on the floor like that and stuff. George had people stand on his chest. Yeah, jump on his chest. What we call that eccentric. So Henry did all that too. Henry done that before George did that. Yeah, sure. Henry was really the originator of it. Well, uh, start. I didn't get that on here. You say Henry could read a good reader, but the rest of you never did learn to read. No, none of us read outside of Henry. Henry would sit down and play first chair in a big 60-piece band.
